Paper · 12 Feb 2026

A small polymerase ribozyme that can synthesize itself and its complementary strand

Gianni, Kwok, Wan, Goeij, Clifton, Colizzi, Attwater, Holliger · Science 391:1022-1028

In a sentence

A 45-letter RNA, QT45, found in random sequences, copies RNA in ice and made both a copy of itself and of its partner strand.

In plain words

RNA-world ideas need an RNA that copies RNA. The known RNA copiers were large, too big to arise by chance. QT45 is only 45 letters long and was fished out of random sequences. Working in slightly alkaline ice and fed three-letter RNA pieces, it copied its partner strand and, with chosen pieces, itself. The yields are tiny, about 0.2% after 72 days, but the find suggests such copiers may be less rare than thought.

Technical detail

QT45 (45 nt) from random pools catalyses general RNA-templated RNA synthesis from trinucleotide triphosphates in mildly alkaline eutectic ice. Complementary-strand synthesis with a random triplet pool at 94.1% per-nucleotide fidelity; self-synthesis with defined substrates; both ~0.2% yield in 72 days. Triplets are pre-activated and supplied. Online 12 Feb 2026, issue dated March 2026.

What we take from it

Planned test

The closest result to the step from template copying (L2) to self-replication (L3). Task #2 extracts its numbers; task #12 seals a prediction for its untested double mutants. The founding plan's second-hand '0.02% over 72 days' was wrong; the paper says about 0.2%.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
